nodes.summary: For probability mass functions $p$ and $q$ on a finite alphabet, the cross-entropy $H(p, q)$ in bits equals $H(p) + D(p \parallel q) / \ln 2$, where $H(p)$ is the Shannon entropy of $p$ in bits and $D(p \parallel q)$ is the Kullback–Leibler divergence of $p$ from $q$ with the natural logarithm. The identity holds in $[0, \infty]$ with no support hypothesis: when $p$ charges an outcome that $q$ rules out, both sides…
nodes.title: Cross-entropy is entropy plus divergence

nodes.summary: For probability mass functions $p$ and $q$ on a finite alphabet, the cross-entropy $H(p, q)$ in bits equals the Shannon entropy $H(p)$ in bits if and only if $q = p$. Thus log loss is a strictly proper scoring rule.
nodes.title: Equality in Gibbs' inequality

nodes.summary: For an outcome $y$ of a finite alphabet and a probability mass function $q$ on it, the cross-entropy $H(\delta_y, q)$ of $q$ relative to the point mass $\delta_y$ at $y$ equals the surprisal $-\log_2 q(y)$ of $y$ under $q$, which is $\infty$ when $q(y) = 0$.
nodes.title: Cross-entropy of a point mass

nodes.summary: For probability mass functions $p$ and $q$ on a finite alphabet, the cross-entropy of $q$ relative to $p$ is $H(p, q) = \sum_a p(a) \cdot (-\log_2 q(a))$ in bits, a value in $[0, \infty]$. Here $-\log_2 q(a)$ is the surprisal of $a$ under $q$, which is $\infty$ when $q(a) = 0$, and a term with $p(a) = 0$ contributes $0$. So $H(p, q)$ is $\infty$ exactly when $p$ charges an outcome that $q$ rules out.
nodes.title: Cross-entropy

nodes.summary: For probability mass functions $p$ and $q$ on a finite alphabet, the expected surprisal $\mathbb{E}_{a \sim p}[-\log_2 q(a)]$ (with $-\log_2 0 = \infty$), taken as the integral of a $[0, \infty]$-valued function with respect to the law $p$, equals the cross-entropy $H(p, q)$.
nodes.title: Cross-entropy is expected surprisal

nodes.summary: The cross-entropy of any prediction `q` is at least the entropy of the truth `p`.
nodes.title: Gibbs' inequality

nodes.summary: For any probability mass function $p$ on a type $\alpha$ and any point $b$ of a finite alphabet $\beta$, the image of $p$ under the constant map $\alpha \to \beta$ with value $b$ has Shannon entropy $0$.
nodes.title: A constant observation has zero entropy

nodes.summary: For a probability mass function $p$ on a finite alphabet $\alpha$ and a bijection $e : \alpha \to \beta$ onto a finite alphabet $\beta$, the image of $p$ under $e$ has the same Shannon entropy as $p$.
nodes.title: Entropy is invariant under relabeling

nodes.summary: For a probability mass function $p$ on a finite alphabet $\alpha$, the image of $p$ under $a \mapsto (a, 0)$ in $\alpha \times \{0\}$ has the same Shannon entropy as $p$.
nodes.title: Appending a singleton coordinate preserves entropy

nodes.summary: For every outcome $a$ of a finite alphabet, the point mass at $a$ has Shannon entropy $0$.
nodes.title: A point mass has zero entropy

nodes.summary: The Shannon entropy in bits of a probability mass function $p$ on a finite type $\alpha$ is $H(p) = -\sum_{a \in \alpha} p(a) \log_2 p(a)$, where a term with $p(a) = 0$ contributes $0$.
nodes.title: Shannon entropy

nodes.summary: The surprisal (information content) in bits of an outcome of probability $q$ is $-\log_2 q$, with value $\infty$ when $q = 0$. Formally $q$ ranges over the extended nonnegative reals $[0, \infty]$: the surprisal of $0$ is $\infty$, the surprisal of $q \in (0, \infty)$ is $\max(0, -\log_2 q)$, and the surprisal of $\infty$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Surprisal

nodes.summary:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be finite measures on a finite type $\alpha$ in which every singleton is measurable, with $\mu \ll 
u$ and $\mu(\alpha) = 
u(\alpha)$. Then the Kullback–Leibler divergence $\mathrm{KL}(\mu \parallel 
u)$, taken as a real number, equals $\sum_{a \in \alpha} \mu(\{a\}) \log (\mu(\{a\}) / 
u(\{a\}))$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm and a term with $\mu(\{a\}) = 0$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Kullback–Leibler divergence on a finite space

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $q$ be probability mass functions on a finite type $\alpha$ in which every singleton is measurable, such that $p(a) = 0$ whenever $q(a) = 0$, and let $P$ and $Q$ be the measures they define. Then the Kullback–Leibler divergence $\mathrm{KL}(P \parallel Q)$, taken as a real number, equals $\sum_{a \in \alpha} p(a) \log (p(a) / q(a))$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm and a term with $p(a) = 0$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Kullback–Leibler divergence of finite probability laws

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
